title: Trump meets love interest at Mogilevich's Moscow hotel
description_short: Trump meets love interest at Mogilevich's Moscow hotel
description_medium: A TrumpFile timeline recounts that Donald Trump attended a party at Moscow’s Baltschug-Kempinski hotel during a November 1996 visit. Its title also alleges that he met a romantic interest there and that the hotel was owned by Semion Mogilevich, but provides no details supporting either claim. A broader Senate inquiry did not verify the anecdote.
description_long: A TrumpFile timeline says Donald Trump attended a party in the “Library” room at Moscow’s Baltschug-Kempinski hotel during a November 1996 visit. The same timeline associates the hotel with Semion Mogilevich and claims Trump met a romantic interest there. The headline’s ownership and personal-encounter claims go beyond the account’s details: it provides no guest list, hotel ownership records or independent confirmation of the meeting. A later Senate Intelligence Committee investigation examined Trump-Russia contacts and business interests, but did not substantiate this specific anecdote. The hotel gathering remains an attributed report; the claims about who owned the property and whom Trump met are unverified.

title: Trump: Jay Clayton tapped by Trump to lead SDNY
description_short: Trump: Jay Clayton tapped by Trump to lead SDNY
description_medium: On November 14, 2024, Trump selected former Securities and Exchange Commission chair Jay Clayton to lead the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York. Reuters described the choice as unconventional because Clayton lacked criminal-law experience and noted questions about potential conflicts tied to his corporate work. The selection was not yet a completed appointment.
description_long: On November 14, 2024, Reuters reported that Trump had selected Jay Clayton, a former chair of the Securities and Exchange Commission, to lead the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York. The office is known for high-profile financial-crime and public-corruption prosecutions. Reuters described Clayton as an unconventional choice because he lacked criminal-law experience. His corporate work also raised questions about possible conflicts if former clients became subjects of investigations or prosecutions. Those concerns were prospective, involving impartiality and possible recusal, not evidence that he would favor a client or interfere with a case. Trump’s selection was a choice for a sensitive prosecutorial post, not a completed appointment. If appointed, Clayton would lead prosecutors whose work could intersect with his previous corporate relationships; how any conflict would be handled would depend on actual cases and appropriate recusal decisions.
organization_tags: U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Jay Clayton tapped by Trump to lead SDNY
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Jay Clayton tapped by Trump to lead SDNY

notes: Reuters’ linked headline and publication date support November 14, 2024 as the selection date; the timeline’s December 5 date was inconsistent. This describes Trump’s selection, not a completed appointment.

title: Imposes Section 201 Tariffs on Solar Panels and Washing Machines
description_short: Trump issued a proclamation imposing safeguard tariffs on imported solar cells and washing machines.
description_medium: On January 23, 2018, President Trump issued a proclamation applying Section 201 safeguard tariffs to imported solar cells and modules and large residential washing machines. The measure covered two product groups: solar equipment and large household washers. Tariff rates, product exclusions and duration would determine which imports faced added costs.
organization_tags: Office of the U.S. Trade Representative

title: Government Shutdown Ends After 35 Days
description_short: Trump agreed to reopen the government after the longest shutdown in U.S. history without securing wall funding.
description_medium: On January 25, 2019, Trump agreed to reopen the federal government after a 35-day shutdown without securing the border-wall funding he had demanded. The agreement ended the immediate closure and left the funding dispute unresolved. The shutdown became the longest in U.S. history, while no permanent agreement on wall funding was reached.

title: Trump's Iran War Justification Faced Fresh Credibility Stress From Independent Commentary
description_short: Trump's Iran War Justification Faced Fresh Credibility Stress From Independent Commentary
description_medium: In a March 2, 2026 opinion piece, Rolling Stone writer Mac William Bishop criticized the Trump administration’s stated rationale for the war in Iran. He argued that officials had shifted their explanation and had not clearly defined the mission’s objectives or end point. His conclusions are commentary, not independent findings about the operation.
description_long: In a March 2, 2026 Rolling Stone opinion piece, Mac William Bishop argued that the administration had not clearly explained its goals or end point for the war in Iran. He contrasted an earlier description of U.S. attacks as having “tot[ally] obliterat[ed]” Iran’s nuclear program with a later argument that Iran was building conventional defenses to protect that program. Bishop treated the shift as a sign of an unclear public rationale and questioned whether airstrikes could force Iran to submit. He also argued that without stated limits, the public could not tell what outcomes would end the operation; that was his interpretation of the administration’s public messaging. The article is an opinion writer’s analysis, not an independent finding about the administration’s intent or military operation. Its case concerns the consistency and clarity of the stated rationale. Bishop framed the debate as a credibility question about the war’s aims.

preserved_fields.description_short: Trump's Iran War Justification Faced Fresh Credibility Stress From Independent Commentary
